lines.text:
Dinner at the New Restaurant

Last Friday, my family went to a new restaurant that opened near our house. We had a reservation for seven o'clock, so we arrived a few minutes early.

The hostess greeted us at the entrance and showed us to our table. It was a corner table with a nice view of the garden. The waiter brought us the menu and a jug of water.

The menu had several sections: starters, main courses, side dishes, and desserts. My father ordered a bowl of soup as a starter. My mother chose a Caesar salad. I decided to have grilled chicken with roasted potatoes and vegetables as my main course. My brother ordered a cheeseburger with chips.

While we waited, the waiter brought a basket of warm bread with olive oil and butter. The food arrived after about twenty minutes. Everything was served on large white plates, and the presentation was beautiful.

The portions were generous, and the food was delicious. My father said the soup was the best he had ever tasted. After the main course, we looked at the dessert menu. I ordered chocolate mousse, and my mother had a slice of cheesecake.

At the end of the meal, the waiter brought the bill. My father paid by card and left a tip. The total was reasonable for the quality of the food.

We all agreed it was a wonderful evening. We will definitely go back.

lines.text: Restaurants in English-speaking countries expect dietary questions: 'Is this gluten-free?', 'Do you have vegan options?', 'Does this contain nuts?' Knowing these phrases is practical.

lines.text: Politeness is essential when ordering. Always say 'please' when ordering and 'thank you' when served. Using 'Could I have...' or 'I'd like...' is more polite than 'I want...' or 'Give me...'.
